# [rev2 F8, F21, rev2.2 R7]; span_pick unit 3.0a, lane s30a): which candidate streams each BUILT search
# feeds. HAND-WRITTEN, never generated from the kit's table. Reader: tests/memfn/rows_check.py section S,
# against `arm_fixtures --streams` (window.c's wf_support): red on a missing, extra or duplicated row, a
# cell that differs, or a RULING row whose quoted sentence is absent from the working-tree ledger file it
# names, which must be an allowed ledger (rows_check.py LEDGERS: memfn/docs/responses.md,
# docs/dev/decisions.md; a sha is provenance only, never looked up; a D-number reads that entry only). A
# RULING row's cells are the ones its quoted sentence states, so the expectation is a ruled line, never the
# table read twice. Its source names the decision record and whose words the line is: "libc memchr supplies
# only one-shot" is a line of the KIT's notice (memfn/docs/responses.md at 067aca4df), which D190
# (docs/dev/decisions.md) files among the owner's decision; it is not the owner's words, so this control
# shares an author with the table (review 2026-11-09 r1 s30a F14). The LIBC rows name D190 as their
# ledger (the kit manager's F14 ruling, lane s30amrg): section S requires the sentence inside that entry. DERIVED rows' basis witnesses are
# landing-time witnesses of 3.0a over base's text (docs/dev/lanes/s30a_report.md).
# Columns: search (a T-FIND pick's name, or `floor`), RESTART, MASK, SHIFT (yes/no), source (`RULING (Dn,
# owner's words|kit-stated line)` or DERIVED), basis (RULING: the sentence in double quotes, then
# `@ LEDGER PROVENANCE`, a sha or the D-number; DERIVED: its basis).
